classification.difficultyReason: Recognise that the leaves are unsorted, order values within each stem, then exclude the central observation and find the two half-medians before subtracting.

content.prompt: The stem-and-leaf plot opposite gives the lengths in centimetres of 15 leaves that have fallen from a tree. The values are given correct to one decimal place. Find the interquartile range of the leaf lengths.

spec.description: Unsorted leaves are individually separated; stem 8 remains empty. The source's tightly printed final 44 beside stem 5 represents two leaves.
spec.answerVisibility: All source data remain visible; no quartiles or answer markings are supplied.

answer.short:
$2.3\text{ cm}$.

Order the leaves before finding the quartiles: $Q_1=5.4\text{ cm}$ and $Q_3=7.7\text{ cm}$.
answer.worked:
In ascending order, the lengths in centimetres are:
$$4.4,\ 5.1,\ 5.4,\ 5.4,\ 5.5,\ 5.8,\ 6.1,\ 6.2,\ 6.3,\ 6.4,\ 7.2,\ 7.7,\ 7.7,\ 9.3,\ 9.4.$$
The median is the eighth value, $6.2$. Omit it when dividing the data into two groups of seven. The median of each group is its fourth value.
$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=5.4\text{ cm}\\Q_3&=7.7\text{ cm}\\\text{IQR}&=Q_3-Q_1\\\text{IQR}&=7.7-5.4\\\text{IQR}&=2.3\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
